section.p: This guide covers runtime management of nginx server blocks via the JavaScript DOM: adding, removing, renaming, and reconfiguring virtual servers, including their SSL configuration.
Prerequisites: read the for single worker guide first for write_mode, snapshot(), and suspendAcceptance(); and the locations guide for addLocation(), removeLocation(), and clone().
Server-level structural operations (add, remove, rename) follow a two-phase model:

stanza.v: srv.setNames([...]) ← server_name list updated in memory
After Phase 1: nginx.http.servers[] reflects the change, but the
server-name hash tables are NOT yet updated. Real HTTP requests
still route according to the OLD hash.
After Phase 2: the server-name hash is rebuilt from all current
nginx.http.servers[]. New requests are dispatched to the updated set.

section.p: This is intentional: it lets you prepare a server completely (add locations, set handler, configure SSL) before any request can reach it.
: addLocation() and removeLocation() (location-level changes) do not require a rebuildVhostDispatch() call — they update the location BST immediately.
Topic │ API
Inspect servers │ nginx.http.servers[], srv.name, srv.names, srv.locations
Add server │ nginx.http.addServer(name [, opts]) + rebuildVhostDispatch()
Remove server │ nginx.http.removeServer(name) + rebuildVhostDispatch()
Clone server │ srv.clone(newName) + rebuildVhostDispatch()
Rename / multi-name │ srv.setNames([…​]) + rebuildVhostDispatch()
Reconfigure properties │ srv.root, srv.clientHeaderTimeout, srv.mergeSlashes, etc.
SSL reconfiguration │ srv.ssl.setCertificate(), ssl.setProtocols(), ssl.setCiphers()
Test routing │ nginx.http.match(uri [, serverName])
Atomicity │ suspendAcceptance(), suspendAllWorkers()

section.p: Creates an independent copy of the server under newName. Unlike addServer(), the clone inherits the full current location tree — all prefix, regex, and named locations (both static and dynamic).
After clone(), the source and clone initially share the underlying ngx_http_core_loc_conf_t C structs for each copied location. This means:
Reading loc.root / loc.handler / etc. on either server returns the same value.
Writing loc.handler = fn via a location object from either server modifies the shared struct and affects both servers.
Calling clone.addLocation('/new/') creates a new, independent entry only in the clone’s BST. It does not affect the source.

To make a location’s config truly independent after cloning, use loc.snapshot() on the clone’s location and then immediately restore() — this forces a copy-on-write. Or set the field you want to differ: the setter will write to the shared struct (which is still correct if you intend to update both), or use write_mode='local' for per-request isolation.

nginx’s server-name dispatch is based on hash tables built at startup. A single atomic rebuild — rather than incremental insertion — avoids hash collisions, wildcard ordering issues, and PCRE regex recompilation during partial updates. The explicit call gives the JS script control over exactly when the new routing becomes active.

title.p: addServer vs srv.clone: location tree sharing

section.p: nginx.http.addServer() always creates an empty location tree. This is deliberate: it forces the caller to explicitly define all locations for the new server, preventing unexpected inheritance of handler functions that may reference per-server state.

srv.clone() copies the full tree for cases where the intent is to create a near-identical virtual host. The initial struct sharing is safe because the clone is not yet reachable until rebuildVhostDispatch() is called, giving the caller a window to customise the clone before any request can reach it.

ssl.setCertificate() replaces the certificate on the live SSL_CTX using SSL_CTX_use_certificate_chain_file / SSL_CTX_use_PrivateKey_file. This is the standard OpenSSL hot-swap path. Sessions established before the swap continue with the old certificate via OpenSSL’s session cache or tickets; only new handshakes use the new certificate.

Each worker maintains its own server-name hash. A rebuildVhostDispatch() call on Worker 0 does not update Workers 1 … N. Broadcast via SharedWorker (see cross-worker section above) is required to synchronise all workers.

rebuildVhostDispatch() logs a warning (NGX_LOG_WARN) and skips duplicate server names silently — it does not throw. The first server registered with a given name wins. Ensure names are unique before calling addServer() if strict routing is required.
